proposal.summary: Proposal only, not an accepted policy decision. Practice and Evaluation modes are asked to operate within the exact same server world identity and topology, and a mid-shift mode transition is to be refused during an active shift so that trajectory integrity, unannounced incident progression and scoring isolation survive. Any training mode switch would require a clean shift restart with a verified roster.

rules.rule: Both Practice and Evaluation modes consume the existing FoundationTrainingMode enum, FoundationSimulationProfile.TrainingMode, and the FoundationWorldSimulation.TrainingMode getter without duplicating enums or creating separate world branches.
In Practice mode, requested guidance responses include the synthetic procedure hint, recommended action and evidence basis tag.
In Evaluation mode, procedure hint fields and step-by-step guidance are strictly excluded from client projections and responses.
Both modes project the same server world identity (WorldId, ShiftId, 13 regions, 12 portals) and differ only in the mode response filtering.

A mid-shift mode transition is refused while the shift is live: the call returns false with the documented blocked reason and does not auto-restart, clear or otherwise mutate the active simulation. A request for the mode already running is an idempotent no-op.
Adding the mode to a projection must not delete the authored geometry status, which the current-location banner and the route synthetic label consume.

blockedReason: Mid-shift mode transition is blocked without an accepted PM policy decision (FMP-11b-D01). Active shift trajectory and scoring fairness require a clean shift restart.
limits: No verifiable PM policy decision ref is linked to this record. It is an unapproved proposal and must not be read as an approved policy decision; approved=false and canonicalWriteAllowed=false above say exactly that.
Implementing a safe default block in code is not evidence that the clean-shift-restart policy itself was approved.
These rules are asserted by tests, not accepted by a human authority. Test assertions are not staff procedure or facility acceptance.
Does not invent official railway procedures or scoring rules.
Provisional synthetic guidance evidence basis only; not surveyed facility or operational acceptance.

verification.platformNote: The assembly definition declares includePlatforms: ["Editor"], which is what makes this an EditMode assembly. The folder name Tests/Editor is not the determinant.
verification.executionNote: No Unity batchmode run was performed by the author of this record; the orchestrator runs Unity. Each rule below records only which test asserts it, never a PASS.

skipPath.statement: The fixture has no self-skip path. The dirty-scene bail-out that could mark the whole fixture skipped was removed and replaced with Assert.Fail, so an unsaved scene fails the run loudly instead of reporting the class as passed-with-zero-executed-assertions.
skipPath.why: docs/context/work-graph.json item 138 checks[0].negativeCase states that a skipped test does not meet acceptance, so a self-skip path is a non-acceptance state and must not exist in the suite.

declaredAcceptanceCommand.reason: FMP11bModeResponseTests lives in ChooGuard.Foundation.Multiplayer.Tests, whose asmdef sets includePlatforms: ["Editor"]. A -testPlatform PlayMode run cannot collect a class from an Editor-only assembly, so this command would report zero tests for the class even when every guard passes. A green run of it is not evidence that any guard in this record holds.
declaredAcceptanceCommand.expectedFieldConflict: checks[0].expected asks PlayMode.xml to record the issue-specific test class as executed. Under the declared platform that expectation is unreachable.

correctAcceptanceCommand.formSource: The EditMode -testFilter form is the repository's own convention; docs/context/work-graph.json carries it for every other EditMode check (for example the FMP-03 and FMP-06a check commands).
correctAcceptanceCommand.note: Recorded here because work-graph.json is not in this unit's write scope (item 138 requiredLocks and writeScope do not list it), so the declared check entry could not be corrected in place. additionalGuards.guard: NetworkFieldRuntime.ApplyProjectedTrainingMode is the single place the outgoing mode is decided, and SendView stamps every client view through it.
additionalGuards.note: This seam replaced the previous inline `TrainingMode = ProjectedTrainingMode(simulation)` initializer at the send site. Before the change a mutation hard-coding Practice at the send site was unreachable by any test, because every test built its own FieldView and called the read-only helper.

additionalGuards.guard: ProjectCurrentLocation stamps the mode on every return path, including the unresolvable-region path.
additionalGuards.note: Before the change the unresolvable-region early return left TrainingMode at the default Practice while ProcedureHintsVisible was false, so an Evaluation session read as Practice for a region it could not resolve.

notVerified: The clean-shift-restart policy itself: no PM decision ref is linked and no authority accepted it.
Any Unity test result: this record's rules are asserted in source only.

That SendView itself cannot be mutated to drop or bypass the seam call: SendView is a private method on a MonoBehaviour reached only through the Unity runtime, so no test outside the Editor can execute it. The seam makes the decision point testable, but the call site that invokes it remains covered only by review.
